You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged — buyer working draft
**Treatment of source material:** The Seller Update and Disclosure Letter are the counterparty's drafts. Nothing in them is treated as agreed, final, market standard or pre-cleared merely because it says so (playbook 0.4 / 6.3).

---

## 1. Headline view

The Seller Update is, in substance, a seller-favourable re-cut of the liability regime dressed as a "fair and balanced package". Almost every limitation point departs from our playbook, and several items are packaged to look like movement toward us when they are not (most notably the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period, which happen to match our *unauthorised* fallbacks). The Disclosure Letter, by contrast, is more useful to us than the covering update — it candidly concedes that key completion deliverables (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, bonus funding, title verification) have **not** been done.

Two framing points before the detail:

- **Two numbers match our fallbacks — that is not clearance.** The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap and the 18-month claims period are our conditional fallbacks, usable only on Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. No such authority has been given. We respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months, and treat the coincidence as a reason for extra caution rather than a shortcut to agreement.
- **The Seller's "settled"/"agreed"/"addressed" language carries no weight.** Tax/IP are described as "settled" — our record shows them OPEN. The funds flow is described as reflecting "agreed price mechanics" — it silently omits AUD 420,000 of bonuses. Bluefen is "addressed" — the letter admits no consent exists.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General warranty cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority (none given).
**Analysis:** The cap is roughly a 20% reduction in our recovery headroom on a deal with live, quantifiable exposures (Bluefen ~30% of revenue; Riverlark AUD 3.2m; Ironquay AUD 180k; bonuses AUD 420k+; an unresolved privacy incident). The seller may well have calibrated to a number they expect us to accept. We do not.
**Push back:** Hold 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is within range. If the team wants to explore 20% as a trade, that requires a written instruction from Amelia Frost identifying this draft before anything is communicated.

### 2.2 Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** This is a 5x increase on both thresholds plus a change in basket mechanics. The excess-only (deductible) basket alone costs us AUD 250,000 off the top of any successful claim set. Combined with the AUD 25,000 de minimis, a realistic cluster of mid-sized operational claims could be rendered wholly unrecoverable. This is a bigger economic shift than the headline cap.
**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Reject the deductible structure outright; it is not a drafting nuance but a different allocation of risk.

### 2.3 Claims period and "all Claims" override — Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none); Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate with no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** Two issues. (a) 18 months is the unauthorised fallback — same treatment as the cap. (b) The second sentence is the more dangerous: it is a catch-all that would pull fundamental, tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims into the general 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and carve out each one. It also interacts with 9.3/12.8/20.5 (below) to make the general regime the default for everything.
**Push back:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence and replace with an express statement that the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants, or fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
**Playbook:** separate regime — 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Capping title at 20% means that if we do not get good title to 100% of the shares, we recover at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m price, and only if we discover it inside 18 months. This is unacceptable on any view.
**Push back:** Full separate regime per playbook. Non-negotiable in substance.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" — Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** blanket application.
**Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; no one may waive this.
**Analysis:** The draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**. Combined with the "all Claims" override in 12.3/13 and the exclusive-remedy/non-reliance language, the seller is attempting to limit liability for its own fraud. Beyond being commercially unacceptable, this is the kind of clause whose enforceability is doubtful — but we should not rely on a court to fix it; we should fix the drafting.
**Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all of Clauses 9, 12, 13 and 20, "to the maximum extent permitted by law". Make clear nothing in the SPA limits liability for the seller's own fraud. This is a playbook red line and not within anyone's authority to trade.

### 2.6 Disclosure — Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]
**Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** [1.1] and [1.2] are exactly the deemed-disclosure mechanisms we reject. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended — it is not limited to ASIC or PPSR, and would arguably deem disclosed anything a search *could* have found. Note also the data room cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is now some six weeks old; any later additions would not even be within the seller's own cut-off, and we should confirm what, if anything, has been added since.
**Push back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosure. Replace with a standard requiring disclosure to be specific, fair and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Permit at most a closed list of specified public searches (named registers, named dates) as disclosed. Confirm data room additions post-22 Sept and require a bring-down.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar — "discoverable" not "known". Read with the general disclosure in [1.1], it means every item in the data room is both deemed disclosed *and* deemed known, closing off recovery twice over. It also extends to advisers, so a line in a DD report that a junior reviewer saw but did not escalate would defeat a claim.
**Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3 in its entirety. Resist any actual-knowledge qualifier unless confined to named individuals on our side with actual knowledge of the specific breach and resulting loss — and even then never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Any *seller* knowledge qualifiers in the warranties must be limited to named seller persons after due and careful enquiry.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
**Disclosure Letter [2]:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); clause 11.2 change-control, conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied** as at letter date.
**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** The Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says it is not done. The "satisfied on delivery" mechanic is the problem: a Bluefen letter that is conditional (as 11.3 contemplates) would trigger the condition while leaving us exposed to the conditions not being met post-Completion. For a customer representing ~30% of revenue, this is deal-critical.
**Push back:** Condition precedent requires (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen under 11.2, or (ii) if conditional, written evidence each 11.3 condition is satisfied, in each case in form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer and not revoked at Completion. Replace "reasonable endeavours" with "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a specific undertaking to pursue and keep us informed. Consider a Bluefen-specific indemnity or price mechanism as backstop if consent slips, but do not accept consent-on-delivery.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility — Clause 2 / 7
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter [3]:** facility not repaid; no final discharge of security in data room; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
**Playbook:** current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, we would be paying full price while the target remains encumbered and in potential change-of-control default under 8.1. The ~AUD 3.2m figure is "approximately" and from a September document — it is not a current payout. A post-completion release is the seller's preferred structure, not ours, and is outside our authority to accept without Amelia Frost.
**Push back:** Require (i) Riverlark payout letter dated no earlier than 2 business days before Completion; (ii) direct payment from Completion funds to Riverlark per the funds flow; (iii) executed deeds of release and PPSR discharge documents delivered at Completion (held in escrow if necessary); (iv) Riverlark confirmation of no change-of-control objection or waiver of 8.1. If the seller insists on post-completion release, that goes to Amelia Frost with an irrevocable lender undertaking in hand — we do not negotiate it at working level.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses and funds flow — DD-005
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow; funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics".
**Disclosure Letter [5]:** bonuses conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in funds flow; **silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs**.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** "A matter for the Seller" is an assertion, not a mechanism. The bonuses are a Company obligation triggered by our Completion; if not funded, the Company (which we then own) pays them, so economically we pay them unless the price or funds flow adjusts. The on-cost silence is a gap — superannuation and payroll tax on AUD 420,000 are material in their own right. Note also that the "agreed price mechanics" characterisation is unverified; we have not agreed a funds flow that omits these.
**Push back:** Insert a specific funds flow line for bonuses plus all employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accruals triggered), funded by the Seller either by direct deduction from the price or by a Seller-funded payment to the Company at Completion. Require a schedule of recipients, amounts and conditions. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Reject any suggestion the funds flow is "agreed" until this is in.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1
**Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Disclosure Letter [4]:** clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
**Playbook:** broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified either way.
**Analysis:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. The seller's indemnity covers the payment, not the ownership gap, nor the costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment, nor any third-party claims or business disruption if Ironquay asserts rights. We should not accept or dispute the AUD 180,000 figure; we should verify it.
**Push back:** Indemnity to cover (i) any amount payable to Ironquay to perfect ownership of all SOW3 Project Materials (not just AUD 180,000); (ii) costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment; (iii) losses from any Ironquay claim or any defect in title to the Project Materials. Preserve the cure: pre-Completion payment and delivery of a confirmatory assignment should be a completion deliverable. Request Ironquay statement of account / bank evidence to confirm the open balance.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6, DD-006
**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter [6]:** download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the seller's own letter says cannot yet be drawn. Equally, we should not overstate it — the facts do not establish a breach, harm or a notification obligation. The correct posture is process, not price, at this stage. The risk is that the general regime (20%/18 months/AUD 25k de minimis) would absorb this if it crystallises into a regulatory matter later.
**Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion undertakings: preserve all access/download logs and the link's access record; complete the investigation (including obtaining link access data from the hosting provider); report findings to Buyer; (ii) bring-down of DD-006 at Completion; (iii) a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party claims), sitting outside the general cap/basket/time limit, with its own period tied to limitation for the relevant regulatory action. Do not quantify a demand; do not accept "not material".

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals — DD-008 / DD-011
**Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs".
**Disclosure Letter [8]:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; read together; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** The seller's label is unsupported by its own disclosure. We should not reflexively treat them as Debt either. The questions are: are these already committed, when do they fall due relative to Completion, are they genuinely recurring operating spend reflected in the forecast, and are any of them pre-paid or accrued (which would affect the working capital or Debt position).
**Push back:** Request the three Sandbar agreements, renewal notices and payment schedules. Reserve position on classification pending review. Ensure the Debt/Working Capital definitions do not pre-empt the point. No price deduction proposed at this stage.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above".
**Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.
**Analysis:** Not settled. Describing them as settled under a regime that itself is unacceptable is a double overreach. Tax and IP need their own regimes (customary tax period tied to the statutory review window; IP period calibrated to the Ironquay and ownership issues).
**Push back:** Record in our response that Tax and IP remain open and are not subject to Clause 12.1–12.3 or the "all Claims" override. Table separate Tax and IP limitation proposals once internally settled. Do not propose unlimited liability.

### 2.15 Title
**Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
**Disclosure Letter [10]:** DD-012 identifies the source relied on; Buyer has not completed own verification.
**Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal source.
**Analysis:** The register is maintained by the Company and supplied by the seller. It is the starting point, not proof. The seller's own letter concedes we have not verified. Combined with the proposal to cap title claims at 20%/18 months, the title package is wholly inadequate.
**Push back:** Obtain and review: current ASIC extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (share charges); Seller's constitution and board resolution authorising the sale; evidence of Seller's own title chain (prior transfers, any options, pre-emptive rights, shareholder agreements); confirmation no escrow, lien or encumbrance over the shares. Require full title/capacity/authority warranties on the fundamental regime (2.4 above).

### 2.16 Lesser items — lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The letter notes the lease has a notification obligation and Mossvale an assignment restriction, in each case stating the material does not say consent is required for a share sale. We should read the underlying clauses ourselves rather than accept the seller's characterisation. Low priority but confirm: (i) is the lease notification pre- or post-Completion, and is there any landlord termination right on change of control; (ii) does Mossvale's clause contain a change-of-control deeming provision. Add warranties that no counterparty consent or notice is required other than as specifically disclosed.

### 2.17 Disclosure Letter [1.4] and [11]
[1.4] is a standard non-admission; acceptable in principle but it must not be read to undercut the specific facts conceded. [11] is useful: the seller expressly disclaims any "expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval". We should quote this back against the Seller Update's "agreed" / "settled" / "addressed" language.

---

## 3. What the Disclosure Letter actually concedes (use this)

| Item | Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter concedes |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No consent; no evidence of conditions satisfied |
| Riverlark | "will be addressed" post-Completion | Not repaid; no discharge documents |
| Bonuses | "matter for the Seller" | Not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | No receipt; no confirmatory assignment; ownership conditional on payment |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification all undetermined |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Disclosure silent on whether ordinary course |
| Title | "evidenced by DD-012" | Buyer has not verified |

These are not matters we need to argue. The seller's own letter establishes them.

---

## 4. Verified vs asserted

**Verified from source documents (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026):** Bluefen revenue and clause references; Riverlark approximate balance and clause references; DD-005 bonus total; DD-006 incident facts as recorded; Sandbar amounts; DD-012 register entry.

**Seller assertions, unverified:** that any position is "agreed", "settled", "addressed", "adequate", "ordinary-course", "not material"; that the funds flow reflects agreed mechanics; that the AUD 180,000 is actually unpaid (or paid); that AUD 3.2m is the current Riverlark payout.

**Stale:** all source material is dated 22 Sept 2026; today is 6 Nov 2026. Request refreshed Riverlark balance, Bluefen status, DD-006 investigation status, Ironquay account, and any data room additions.

**Authority flags:** 20% cap and 18-month period require Amelia Frost written authority — none exists. Post-completion Riverlark release requires Amelia Frost approval — none exists. Fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Red lines (no authority to move):**
1. Full fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
2. Fundamental/Title on separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
3. Delete the "all Claims" override (12.3/13) and the blanket application in 9.3/12.8/20.5; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant regimes separate.

**Hold at playbook opening positions (fallbacks not authorised):**
4. General cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
5. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
6. General claims period 24 months.

**Delete / replace:**
7. General disclosure [1.1], [1.2] and Schedule 7 — specific fair disclosure only; closed list of named searches at most.
8. Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge — delete entirely.

**Completion mechanics:**
9. Bluefen: unconditional consent or evidenced satisfaction of 11.3 conditions as a CP; no consent-on-delivery; stronger endeavours covenant.
10. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases and PPSR discharges at Completion. Post-completion release only via Amelia Frost with irrevocable lender undertaking.
11. Bonuses: specific funds flow line for AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs, seller-funded, with indemnity for shortfall. Reject "agreed funds flow" characterisation.

**Specific indemnities / investigation:**
12. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to cover perfecting ownership of all SOW3 Project Materials and related losses; preserve pre-Completion cure; verify the AUD 180,000.
13. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, bring-down, and a standalone indemnity outside the general regime. No quantification; no acceptance of "not material".

**Reserve / investigate:**
14. Sandbar: obtain agreements; reserve classification; no price deduction yet.
15. Tax / IP: state expressly OPEN; table separate regimes; no unlimited liability.
16. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional/authority evidence; DD-012 is not proof.
17. Lease and Mossvale: read underlying clauses; add no-consent-required warranties.

**Process:**
18. Respond to the covering letter noting that nothing is agreed, settled or addressed, citing the seller's own [11]; request refreshed source facts for all time-sensitive items given the 22 Sept cut-off.
19. Confirm internally with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been given before any counter is sent, so no one on our side treats the 20%/18-month coincidence as cleared.

I can turn this into a formal mark-up of the Seller Update or a response letter if that is the next step.
=== END ADVICE ===
